title: Atolia / Atesis copper corridor hypothesis v0

claim.measure: gross mass crossing the Atesis trunk checkpoint once per downstream passage
claim.interpretation: Corridor throughput, not an estimate of copper mined inside the Adige basin. Source composition is latent and must be reconstructed.

time_prior_note: The 200,000 t total is fixed by the scenario. The phase split is a v0 prior chosen to place most throughput after the sixteenth century BC and must remain editable rather than being presented as an archaeological measurement.
geometry_note: The first overlay uses the modern Adige/Athesis hydrological trunk as a carrier skeleton. It is not a reconstruction of every Bronze Age palaeochannel, delta branch, landing place or navigability limit.

evidence_anchors.label: Mitterberg scale comparator
evidence_anchors.role: external production-scale comparator; not assumed to feed the Atesis
evidence_anchors.source: Pernicka, Lutz & Stoellner, Bronze Age Copper Produced at Mitterberg and its Distribution

evidence_anchors.label: Eastern Trentino smelting field
evidence_anchors.role: real production-field prior; exact contribution to Atesis flow remains latent
evidence_anchors.source: Bellintani et al., Prehistoric copper production in Trentino

evidence_anchors.label: Acqua Fredda / Redebus Pass
evidence_anchors.source: Deutsches Bergbau-Museum, Praehistorische Kupferproduktion in Trentino Orientale

evidence_anchors.label: Frattesina redistribution node
evidence_anchors.role: late trans-shipment / manufacturing comparator near the Po-Adriatic system
evidence_anchors.source: Pearce, Bellintani & Nicolis, Frattesina and the later Bronze Age–Early Iron Age metals trade

tests: Can known and plausible source fields supply the required trunk flow without impossible mine output?
Does the implied slag, charcoal, timber and labour footprint fit the archaeological landscape?
Do trace-element and isotope mixtures downstream require multiple source fields or heavy recycling?
Do workshop lineages and object distributions follow the river corridor more strongly than alternative least-cost routes?
Can the high-throughput scenario be distinguished from a 20,000–60,000 t null world after preservation and excavation bias?
